movement.description: SFB uses a proportional movement system where all ships move simultaneously. A ship's speed determines which of the 32 impulses it moves on. Movement is resolved on a hex grid.

speedSystem.description: Speed determines how often a ship moves during a turn. A speed-32 ship moves on every impulse except impulse 1. A speed-1 ship moves only on impulse 32.

movementChart.description: The 32-Impulse Movement Chart maps speed to impulses. At a given speed, a ship moves on specific impulses determined by the chart. Impulse 1: no units move (speed 31 or less). Impulse 32: all units move.
movementChart.impulse1: No units move (starships restricted to speed 31 or less). Speed-32 seeking weapons one hex from targets hit automatically.
movementChart.impulse32: All units move, including the slowest. Targets at range limit of overloaded torpedoes (8 hexes) cannot escape.

speedToImpulses.description: Example impulse mappings for key speeds. Full chart has 32 speeds.

energyCost.description: Higher speeds require more warp engine energy. The cost increases with speed.

costTable.description: Energy cost per speed level (warp engine boxes required).

turnModes.description: Ships change facing (heading) using turn modes. Each mode allows a different amount of turning per turn.

modes.name: Mode 1 — Sharp Turn
modes.description: Standard turn. Ship turns 60 degrees left or right over the course of the turn.

modes.name: Mode 2 — Moderate Turn
modes.description: Ship turns 120 degrees over the turn. Moves in a wider arc.

modes.name: Mode 3 — Wide Turn
modes.description: Ship turns 180 degrees over the turn. Effectively a U-turn spread across the turn.

specialManeuvers.name: Sideslip
specialManeuvers.description: A tactical maneuver where a ship moves laterally while maintaining its facing. Allows repositioning without turning.
specialManeuvers.restrictions: Cannot be used at certain speeds. Requires specific impulse timing.

specialManeuvers.name: High Energy Turn (HET)
specialManeuvers.description: A drastic turning maneuver that allows a ship to turn more than normal. Carries a risk of Breakdown.
specialManeuvers.risk: Breakdown — if the breakdown check fails, the ship suffers a penalty and may lose movement for the turn.

specialManeuvers.name: Quick Reverse
specialManeuvers.description: A ship can reverse direction quickly, but at reduced speed and with Breakdown risk.

specialManeuvers.name: Acceleration / Deceleration
specialManeuvers.description: Ships can change speed mid-turn, but acceleration and deceleration are limited. Changing speed affects which impulses the ship moves on.
specialManeuvers.restrictions: Mid-turn speed changes are optional rules in some editions.

breakdown.description: When a ship attempts a risky maneuver (HET, Quick Reverse), it must pass a Breakdown check. Failure means the ship suffers a Breakdown penalty.
effects: Ship may lose movement for the current turn
Ship may be forced to a lower speed
Breakdown Rating on the SSD determines vulnerability

separation.description: Ships must maintain minimum separation. Two ships cannot occupy the same hex. Collision rules apply if ships end up in the same hex.

zoneOfControl.description: In campaign play, ships exert a Zone of Control (ZoC) that restricts enemy movement. In tactical play, certain weapons and terrain create ZoC effects.

sublightMovement.description: Shuttles, fighters, and patrol fighters (PFs) have their own movement rules. They can move at higher speeds relative to their size.
sublightMovement.maxSpeed: PFs and Interceptors may move at a maximum speed of 6 hexes.

shuttles.description: Small transport vessels with simplified movement rules.
shuttles.energy: Shuttles do not fill out an Energy Allocation Form. Their engine provides energy to move and fire their phaser.

speed.description: Administrative shuttles have a maximum speed of 6 hexes per turn. Must announce speed at start of each turn and remain at this speed for the entire turn. If no speed is announced, maximum speed is assumed.
speed.acceleration: A shuttle may accelerate by up to one-half of its maximum movement (round up) at the start of a given turn (up to its maximum speed). May be launched at its maximum speed.

uses: Wild Weasel decoys to attract seeking weapons
Suicide shuttles charged with anti-matter bombs
restrictions: Destroyed if towed at high speed

fighters.description: Sublight combat aircraft launched from carriers.

speed.description: Fighters move at sublight speeds, typically up to 6 hexes per turn.

types.description: Basic fighter with phaser weapons. Used for combat and interception.
Fast fighter designed specifically to intercept seeking weapons (drones and plasma torpedoes).

restrictions: Require carrier or base for launch and recovery
Cannot operate without supporting unit in campaign play

patrolFighters.description: Fast Patrol Ships (PFs) — small, fast sublight vessels.

speed.description: PFs move at sublight speeds, typically up to 6 hexes per turn.

restrictions: Cannot operate without supporting unit in campaign play

acceleration.description: Ships can change speed between turns, but acceleration is limited.
rules: A ship may accelerate by up to 4 points per turn (from previous turn's speed).
After performing tactical maneuvers, the ship is considered to have had a speed of 'zero' for acceleration purposes.
The count of hexes for the turn and sideslip modes are reset to zero after tactical maneuvers.

sideslip.description: A tactical maneuver where a ship moves laterally while maintaining its facing.
rules: Cannot be used at certain speeds.
The sideslip count of hexes is reset after tactical maneuvers.
